query: Thursday's Seminar Thursday. The first-year stands at the seminar lectern with her paper in both hands and no voice at all. A dozen students wait. The lecturer looks at the clock. Her eyes find you at the back of the room. Stand up and argue with her paper You stand and say her fourth paragraph is wrong. It isn't, and she knows it, and she's so annoyed she forgets to be frightened. She takes your objection apart for ten minutes. The room applauds, mostly for her. You stand and object, and your objection is bad, and she's too polite to say so out loud. She sits down without reading. Your essay comes back that week with one line of red: "Good try. Bad argument." Offer to read it for her You walk to the front and hold out your hand. She shakes her head, then gives you the first page. You read the first paragraph aloud. She takes the second page back, and reads the rest herself, quietly, all the way to the end.

results.excerpt:
Hm.
Thorne has handed {o}'s essay back for the third week running, more red ink than black. "Hm," he said, which is all he said. {o} is close to tears in the corridor. "He hates me. He doesn't do this to anyone else. Will you talk to him? He listens to you."
